learningObjectives: Identify the default control types and theme configuration options for Pega UI elements.
Configure dynamic attributes (Visible, Disabled, Required) on UI elements using conditions and When Rules.

elements.description: Pega automatically pairs each field with an appropriate control type based on the field's data type. The 6 defaults are: Autocomplete controls, Check boxes, Drop-down lists, Links, Rich-text editors, Text input. Note: Radio buttons are NOT in this list.

Themes configure the STYLING of UI elements — buttons, links, headers. The out-of-the-box theme is Pegasus. Configure themes in App Studio at Settings → Themes. Themes control appearance only, not behavior.

elements.text: Dynamic UI is like a smart insurance application form. If you answer 'No' to 'Do you own a vehicle?', the entire vehicle section disappears. If you select 'Text' as your preferred contact, the mobile number field becomes required. The form adapts in real time — no page reload needed.

elements.description: Designing UI elements to adapt according to user choices. Provides: real-time response to end-user behavior, robust functionality for most interactions, reduced visual clutter, and fewer full-page refreshes for improved responsiveness.

Default: Always. Options: Always | Never | Custom Condition (short expressions including When Rules) | When Rule (complex/reusable conditions) | If not blank (shows when field has a value) | If not zero (shows when value is non-zero).

Default: Never. Options: Never | Always (always read-only) | Custom Condition (disabled when expression is true) | When Rule (disabled when When Rule returns true). 'If not blank' and 'If not zero' are NOT available here.

Default: Never (optional). Options: Never | Always | Custom Condition (required when expression is true) | When Rule (required when When Rule returns true). 'If not blank' and 'If not zero' are NOT available here.
Custom Condition: for SHORT, one-off expressions (e.g., check one dropdown value). When Rule: for COMPLEX or REUSABLE conditions shared across multiple forms. Both are available for all 3 attributes.

elements.term: 'If not blank' and 'If not zero' — Visible ONLY
elements.description: 'If not blank' shows an element only when the field value is not blank. 'If not zero' shows when the value is not zero. These options appear ONLY under the Visible attribute — not under Disabled or Required.

examPitfalls.title: Know the three defaults: Visible=Always, Disabled=Never, Required=Never
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Questions ask candidates to fill in the default setting for the Disabled or Required attribute. Candidates guess 'Always' for all three, not knowing only Visible defaults to Always while both Disabled and Required default to Never.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Visible defaults to Always (elements show by default). Disabled defaults to Never (elements are editable by default). Required defaults to Never (fields are optional by default).

examPitfalls.title: Custom Condition = short one-off; When Rule = complex or reusable
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Questions describe a visibility condition and ask whether to use a Custom Condition or a When Rule. Candidates always choose Custom Condition. Use Custom Condition for simple, one-time expressions; use a When Rule when the logic is complex, reused in multiple places, or needs to be tested independently.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Custom Condition is for short, simple expressions. When Rule is for complex conditions intended for reuse across multiple forms.

examPitfalls.title: 'If not blank' and 'If not zero' are Visible-only — not for Disabled or Required
examPitfalls.trapDescription: A question asks which conditions are available for the Required attribute. Candidates select 'If not blank' — unaware this built-in condition exists only in the Visible attribute's drop-down and is absent from Disabled and Required.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: 'If not blank' and 'If not zero' are ONLY available as Visible options. They do not appear under Disabled or Required.

examPitfalls.title: Themes = styling only — not behavior
examPitfalls.trapDescription: A scenario asks which feature controls field visibility. Candidates select Theme because themes affect the UI — but themes handle only colors and fonts, never behavioral conditions like Visible, Disabled, or Required.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Themes configure the APPEARANCE of UI elements (buttons, links, headers). Dynamic attributes (Visible, Disabled, Required) control element behavior. These are separate concerns.

examPitfalls.title: Dynamic UI reduces full-page refreshes — not eliminates them
examPitfalls.trapDescription: An exam statement says dynamic UI 'eliminates all full-page refreshes.' Candidates mark it correct because they associate dynamic UI with a smoother experience. The correct claim is 'reduces' — not 'eliminates.'
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Dynamic UI REDUCES full-page refreshes, improving responsiveness. It does not eliminate all page refreshes.

examPitfalls.title: Radio buttons are NOT in the 6 default control types
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Questions list 7 control types and ask which are Pega's 6 defaults. Candidates include Radio buttons — a familiar HTML control — but it is not in Pega's standard 6. Know the actual 6: Autocomplete, Button, Checkbox, Date, Grid, Text.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: The 6 defaults are: Autocomplete, Check boxes, Drop-down lists, Links, Rich-text editors, Text input. Radio buttons are not a default control type.

examPitfalls.title: Custom Condition and When Rule are available for ALL 3 dynamic attributes
examPitfalls.trapDescription: A question asks which condition options apply to the Required attribute. Candidates select only 'Custom Condition,' missing that When Rule is also available for all three attributes — Visible, Disabled, and Required.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Custom Condition and When Rule are available for ALL THREE attributes: Visible, Disabled, and Required.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What is the default visibility setting for a newly added UI element in Pega Platform?
practiceQuiz.hint: Recall the default visibility setting assigned to a newly added UI element in Pega Platform.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Every UI element in a Pega form has a Visible property that controls when it appears. The default value is 'Always,' meaning the element is visible at all times with no condition applied. Setting it to 'Never' would permanently hide it; 'When Rule' or 'Custom Condition' enables conditional visibility based on Case data at runtime.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What is the default disabled setting for UI elements in Pega Platform?
practiceQuiz.hint: By default, users can always interact with elements.
practiceQuiz.rationale: By default, every interactive UI element in Pega has its Disabled property set to 'Never,' meaning users can always interact with it. Setting Disabled to 'Always' makes the element permanently read-only for all users regardless of conditions. 'When Rule' or 'Custom Condition' allows conditional disabling based on specific Case data values at runtime.

practiceQuiz.scenario: You have a complex visibility condition that will be reused across multiple forms. Which visibility setting should you use?
practiceQuiz.hint: Reusable, complex conditional logic that can be referenced across the application = When Rule.
practiceQuiz.rationale: When Rule is for complex or reusable conditions. Custom Condition is for short, one-off expressions. 'If not blank' only checks if a field has a value — not suitable for complex conditions.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A 'Next appointment date' field should only appear after the user has entered a value in it. Which visibility setting achieves this most directly?
practiceQuiz.hint: One option is specific to whether a field has a value.
practiceQuiz.rationale: 'If not blank' shows the UI element only when the field value is not blank — exactly the requirement. A Custom Condition or When Rule would work too but 'If not blank' is the most direct option.

practiceQuiz.scenario: After a customer selects an Account Type, the field should be permanently read-only for the rest of the Case. Which disabled setting should you use?
practiceQuiz.hint: Which default setting means the attribute is permanently applied without any condition?
practiceQuiz.rationale: Pega's Disabled setting for UI elements has four options: 'Never' (always editable — the default), 'Always' (permanently read-only for all users), 'When Rule' (conditionally disabled based on a named When Rule evaluation), and 'Custom Condition' (disabled based on an inline expression). Understanding these four options is essential for designing dynamic, role-appropriate forms.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which THREE are listed benefits of using dynamic UI functionality in Pega?

options.text: Reduced visual clutter on the screen
Automatic field validation without When Rules

practiceQuiz.hint: One listed option is NOT a documented benefit of the Constellation architecture — which?
practiceQuiz.rationale: Dynamic UI benefits: real-time response (A), reduced visual clutter (B), fewer full-page refreshes (C). Automatic field validation without When Rules (D) is not a documented benefit.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which tool is used to configure the styling of UI elements (colors, fonts, button styles) in Pega Platform?
practiceQuiz.hint: The out-of-the-box Constellation design system theme example is called Pegasus.
practiceQuiz.rationale: In Pega Constellation applications, the visual styling of UI elements — colors, typography, spacing — is controlled by Themes, not When Rules or dynamic attributes. The default out-of-the-box theme is Pegasus. When Rules and Conditions control behavioral aspects such as visibility and disabled state, but they have no effect on the visual presentation of the element.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which of the following is NOT one of Pega's 6 default control types?
practiceQuiz.hint: The 6 defaults include Check boxes but not their close relative.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Pega Platform provides six default UI control types out of the box: Autocomplete, Check boxes, Drop-down lists, Links, Rich-text editors, and Text input. Radio buttons are notably absent from this default set — they are not included. Knowing exactly which six types are built-in versus which require custom configuration is a frequently tested exam point.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A 'Cosigner information' section should appear only when the applicant's age is under 21. This condition will be reused on several forms. Which visibility setting is most appropriate?
practiceQuiz.hint: Complex condition that needs to be reused in multiple places = When Rule.
practiceQuiz.rationale: When Rule is appropriate for complex conditions intended for reuse across multiple forms. 'If not blank' and 'If not zero' only check field value state — they cannot evaluate age conditions.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A 'Mobile number' field must be required only when the user selects 'Text' as their preferred contact method. This is a simple, form-specific condition. Which required setting should you use?
practiceQuiz.hint: Simple one-off condition that is not reused elsewhere = Custom Condition, not When Rule.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Custom Condition makes a field required when a specific short expression is true — ideal for simple logic like checking one dropdown value. When Rule would be used if the condition were complex or shared across forms. D ('If not blank') is only available for Visible.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which dynamic attribute options are shared across ALL THREE attributes — Visible, Disabled, and Required?

options.text: If not blank and If not zero
When Rule and If not blank

practiceQuiz.hint: 'If not blank' and 'If not zero' are Visible-only.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Custom Condition and When Rule are available for Visible, Disabled, AND Required. 'If not blank' and 'If not zero' are Visibility-only options — they do not appear under Disabled or Required.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What is the default Required setting for UI elements, and what does it mean?

options.text: Never — users can proceed without entering a value
Always — users must enter a value to proceed
Custom Condition — required only when a condition is met
When Rule — required based on a configurable When Rule

practiceQuiz.hint: Recall the default Required setting for a UI element and what it means for user input.
practiceQuiz.rationale: By default, UI elements are Never required — users can proceed with Case processing without entering a value. They are optional unless explicitly configured otherwise.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An SA is configuring dynamic attributes on a Claims form in Pega Constellation. Which TWO dynamic attributes can be applied to a UI element using a When Rule or condition?

options.text: Visible — controls whether the element is shown or hidden based on a condition evaluated at runtime
Disabled — controls whether the element is interactive (editable) or read-only based on a condition
Font-size — dynamically adjusts the text size of the element based on user role or screen size
Z-Index — controls the visual stacking order of overlapping elements at runtime based on urgency

practiceQuiz.hint: The three dynamic attributes in Pega Constellation are Visible, Disabled, and Required — not CSS properties.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Pega Constellation supports three dynamic attributes on UI elements: Visible (show/hide), Disabled (editable/read-only), and Required (mandatory/optional), each configurable with a When Rule or condition expression. CSS properties like font-size and z-index are not dynamic attributes configurable in Pega's UI configuration layer.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An SA is designing a Claims form where the 'Injury Description' field should only appear when the claim type is 'Personal Injury.' Which TWO elements are needed to implement this conditional visibility?

options.text: A When Rule or condition expression that evaluates whether the claim type equals 'Personal Injury'
The Visible dynamic attribute on the 'Injury Description' field, configured to reference the When Rule
A Decision Table that changes the field's background color to transparent when the condition is false
A separate View for each claim type to avoid using conditional visibility configuration

practiceQuiz.hint: Conditional visibility needs a condition/When Rule and the Visible attribute on the field linked to it.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Conditional visibility requires two elements: the condition logic (a When Rule or inline expression evaluating the claim type) and the Visible attribute on the target field referencing that condition. When the condition is false, the field is hidden. Decision Tables and separate Views are not required or appropriate for this use case.

quickRecap.value: Autocomplete, Check boxes, Drop-down lists, Links, Rich-text editors, Text input. Radio buttons are NOT included.
Configure styling (buttons, links, headers). Out-of-the-box: Pegasus. App Studio → Settings → Themes.
Real-time response, reduced visual clutter, fewer full-page refreshes.
Visible = Always. Disabled = Never. Required = Never.
'If not blank' and 'If not zero' — only for Visible attribute, NOT available for Disabled or Required.
Custom Condition = short one-off expressions. When Rule = complex or reusable conditions.
Custom Condition and When Rule are available for Visible, Disabled, AND Required.
